text.p: Germany's Sandra Voelker broke her own European short-course record to upstage defending champion Le Jingyi of China in the women's 50 metres freestyle heats at the world short-course championships on Friday.

Voelker, silver medallist behind American Jenny Thompson in Thursday's 100 metres freestyle, sped home in 24.62 seconds to slice 0.05 seconds from the mark she set at the European short-course swimming championships in Rostock on December 14 last year.
Thompson won her heat in 25.01, the second-fastest time overall ahead of the evening's final in the Scandinavium indoor arena.
Le, who had to settle for the bronze in her 100 freestyle defence on Thursday, finished second behind Voelker in the final heat and third overall in 25.05.

Le set the current world record of 24.23 at the inaugural world short-course championships in Palma de Mallorca in December 1993. She won both the 50 and 100 freestyle at the 1993 and 1995 editions of the meeting.
